--- title: "[QuantileFamily]{.doc-object-name .doc-class .doc-label .doc-label-class}" body-classes: doc-api-page page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Quantile regression via the Extended Log-F (ELF) pseudo-family. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/feat-psis-loo/whittaker/families/quantile.py#L34-L444){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.CLASS} ```python QuantileFamily(tau=0.5, sigma=1.0) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} `QuantileFamily` fits a single conditional quantile `tau` of the response — for example the median (`tau=0.5`) or the 90th percentile (`tau=0.9`) — rather than the conditional mean targeted by families such as `Gaussian` or `Gamma`. This is useful whenever the object of interest is not the average behavior of the response but a specific point in its distribution, e.g. modeling the upper tail of a skewed cost distribution, or building prediction bands by fitting several quantiles (`tau` values) side by side. Rather than the non-smooth pinball ("check") loss used by classical quantile regression, Whittaker uses the smooth Extended Log-F (ELF) approximation of Fasiolo et al. (2021), which is differentiable and therefore fits within the standard P-IRLS loop via a custom `irls_update`. To fit several quantiles jointly with a shared smoothness structure, fit one `QuantileFamily` per `tau` and compare/combine the resulting models, or see `ConformalPredictor` for distribution-free coverage guarantees around a fitted mean model. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [tau]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[0.5]{.fl}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Quantile level to estimate, in `(0, 1)`. `tau=0.5` corresponds to median regression; smaller values target lower quantiles and larger values target upper quantiles. [sigma]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[1.0]{.fl}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Bandwidth (smoothing) parameter controlling how closely the ELF loss approximates the non-smooth pinball loss. Smaller values give a sharper, more faithful approximation to the pinball loss (and to the check-function optimum) but a less smooth optimization surface; larger values give a smoother but more biased approximation. `sigma` may be adjusted after construction via the `sigma` property, e.g. to anneal it across fitting iterations. ::: ## Notes {.doc-notes} `QuantileFamily` has no meaningful link or variance function in the usual GLM sense — `link` and `link_inverse` are the identity on `eta` — because fitting instead minimizes the ELF loss directly. For a residual `r = y - mu`, the ELF loss is $$ \rho_{\tau,\sigma}(r) = \tau r + \sigma \log\!\left(1 + e^{-r/\sigma}\right), $$ which converges to the pinball loss $\rho_\tau(r) = \tau r \, \mathbb{1}[r \ge 0] - (1-\tau) r \, \mathbb{1}[r < 0]$ as $\sigma \to 0$. Its first and second derivatives with respect to `mu`, $$ \frac{\partial \rho}{\partial \mu} = -\left[\tau - 1 + \operatorname{expit}(r/\sigma)\right], \qquad \frac{\partial^2 \rho}{\partial \mu^2} = \frac{1}{\sigma}\, s (1 - s), \quad s = \operatorname{expit}(r/\sigma), $$ supply the working response `z` and working weight `W` used by the custom `irls_update`. The reported "deviance" is `2 * sum(ELF loss)`, so that it reduces to twice the usual pinball loss in the limit `sigma -> 0`. ## Examples {.doc-examples} Fit the 10th, 50th, and 90th percentile curves of a heteroscedastic response: ::: {#f87b8fd3 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import numpy as np import whittaker as wk rng = np.random.default_rng(0) n = 300 x = np.linspace(0, 2 * np.pi, n) mu = np.sin(x) noise_scale = 0.2 + 0.3 * np.abs(np.cos(x)) y = mu + rng.normal(0, noise_scale, n) data = {"x": x, "y": y} for tau in (0.1, 0.5, 0.9): model = wk.GAM("y ~ s(x)", family=wk.QuantileFamily(tau=tau)) model.fit(data, method="REML") print(f"tau={tau}:") print(model.summary()) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` tau=0.1: GAM fit summary Attributes {.doc-attributes}
Name Description
scale_known Whether the dispersion (scale) parameter is fixed rather than estimated.
sigma Bandwidth parameter `sigma` of the ELF loss approximation.
tau Quantile level `tau` being estimated.
### [scale_known]{.doc-object-name .doc-attribute .doc-label .doc-label-property} ::: {.doc-subject} Whether the dispersion (scale) parameter is fixed rather than estimated. ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-attribute} [scale_known]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} ::: ::: {.doc-text} Always True for `QuantileFamily`, since the ELF loss has no free scale parameter to estimate. ::: ### [sigma]{.doc-object-name .doc-attribute .doc-label .doc-label-property} ::: {.doc-subject} Bandwidth parameter `sigma` of the ELF loss approximation. ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-attribute} [sigma]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} ::: ### [tau]{.doc-object-name .doc-attribute .doc-label .doc-label-property} ::: {.doc-subject} Quantile level `tau` being estimated. ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-attribute} [tau]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} ::: ## Methods {.doc-methods}
Name Description
deviance() Total deviance, twice the summed ELF loss over observations.
initialize() Initialize the mean `mu` from the observed response `y`.
irls_update() Compute the working response and weight for one custom IRLS step.
link() Identity link: map the mean `mu` directly to the linear predictor `eta`.
link_derivative() Derivative of the identity link with respect to `mu`.
link_inverse() Identity inverse link: map the linear predictor `eta` back to `mu`.
log_likelihood() Pseudo log-likelihood implied by the ELF loss.
simulate() Draw random samples from the Asymmetric Laplace distribution.
unit_deviance() Per-observation deviance contribution, twice the ELF loss.
variance() Variance function for `QuantileFamily`, identically equal to 1.
### [deviance()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Total deviance, twice the summed ELF loss over observations. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/feat-psis-loo/whittaker/families/quantile.py#L279-L310){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python deviance(y, mu, *, weights=None) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Implements the family-specific deviance as $$ D = 2 \sum_i w_i\, \rho_{\tau,\sigma}(y_i - \mu_i), $$ where `w_i` are optional observation weights (defaulting to 1) and `rho` is the ELF loss. As `sigma -> 0` this converges to twice the usual pinball loss, matching the deviance convention used by other families. ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [y]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Observed response values. [mu]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Fitted mean values. [weights]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [NDArray or None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional observation weights. If None, all weights are treated as 1. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The total (weighted) deviance. ::: ### [initialize()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Initialize the mean `mu` from the observed response `y`. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/feat-psis-loo/whittaker/families/quantile.py#L424-L441){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python initialize(y) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Implements the family-specific starting values for P-IRLS as a direct copy of the observed response, `mu = y`, which is a reasonable starting point for quantile fitting regardless of `tau`. ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [y]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Observed response values. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Copy of `y`, used as the initial mean estimate. ::: ### [irls_update()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Compute the working response and weight for one custom IRLS step. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/feat-psis-loo/whittaker/families/quantile.py#L241-L277){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python irls_update(y, mu, eta) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Implements the family-specific IRLS update used in place of the standard GLM working response/weight pair, since the ELF loss does not come from an exponential-family model. For residual `r = y - mu`, the update uses the ELF score and curvature $$ u = \tau - 1 + \operatorname{expit}(r/\sigma), \qquad W = \max\!\left(\frac{1}{\sigma}\, s(1-s),\ \epsilon\right), \quad s = \operatorname{expit}(r/\sigma), $$ where `epsilon` is a small floor that prevents zero weights, and forms the working response `z = eta + u / W`. ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [y]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Observed response values. [mu]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Current fitted mean values. [eta]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Current linear predictor values. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [tuple[NDArray, NDArray]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The working response `z` and working weight `W`, both with the same shape as `y`. ::: ### [link()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Identity link: map the mean `mu` directly to the linear predictor `eta`. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/feat-psis-loo/whittaker/families/quantile.py#L164-L182){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python link(mu) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} `QuantileFamily` does not use a link function in the usual GLM sense because it minimizes the ELF loss directly rather than modeling a mean-variance relationship, so this implements the family-specific link as the identity, `eta = mu`. ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [mu]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Mean values on the response scale. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Same values, unchanged, interpreted as the linear predictor `eta`. ::: ### [link_derivative()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Derivative of the identity link with respect to `mu`. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/feat-psis-loo/whittaker/families/quantile.py#L202-L219){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python link_derivative(mu) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Since `link` is the identity, `d(eta)/d(mu) = 1` everywhere, so this implements the family-specific derivative as an array of ones with the same shape as `mu`. ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [mu]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Mean values on the response scale. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Array of ones, same shape as `mu`. ::: ### [link_inverse()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Identity inverse link: map the linear predictor `eta` back to `mu`. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/feat-psis-loo/whittaker/families/quantile.py#L184-L200){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python link_inverse(eta) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Implements the family-specific inverse link as the identity, `mu = eta`, matching `link` above. ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [eta]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Linear predictor values. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Same values, unchanged, interpreted as the mean `mu`. ::: ### [log_likelihood()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Pseudo log-likelihood implied by the ELF loss. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/feat-psis-loo/whittaker/families/quantile.py#L333-L370){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python log_likelihood(y, mu, scale, *, weights=None) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Implements the family-specific log-likelihood as the negative summed ELF loss, $$ \ell = -\sum_i w_i\, \rho_{\tau,\sigma}(y_i - \mu_i), $$ with optional observation weights `w_i`. This is a pseudo-likelihood used for model comparison (e.g. AIC) rather than a true likelihood, since `QuantileFamily` does not correspond to a proper probability model; the `scale` argument is accepted for interface compatibility but unused because `scale_known` is always True. ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [y]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Observed response values. [mu]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Fitted mean values. [scale]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Dispersion parameter; unused since the ELF loss has no free scale. [weights]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [NDArray or None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional observation weights. If None, all weights are treated as 1. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The (weighted) pseudo log-likelihood. ::: ### [simulate()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Draw random samples from the Asymmetric Laplace distribution. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/feat-psis-loo/whittaker/families/quantile.py#L386-L422){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python simulate(mu, scale, rng) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Implements the family-specific sampler by inverting the CDF of the Asymmetric Laplace distribution with location `mu`, scale `sigma`, and asymmetry `tau` — the distribution whose negative log-density is proportional to the pinball loss that the ELF loss approximates. Draws `u ~ Uniform(0, 1)` and returns $$ y = \begin{cases} \mu + \sigma \log(u / \tau), & u < \tau, \\ \mu - \sigma \log\!\left(\dfrac{1-u}{1-\tau}\right), & u \ge \tau. \end{cases} $$ ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [mu]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Location (fitted mean) values. [scale]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Dispersion parameter; unused since sampling instead uses `sigma`. [rng]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [object]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Random number generator exposing a `uniform(size=...)` method. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Simulated response values, same shape as `mu`. ::: ### [unit_deviance()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Per-observation deviance contribution, twice the ELF loss. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/feat-psis-loo/whittaker/families/quantile.py#L312-L331){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python unit_deviance(y, mu) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Implements the family-specific unit deviance as $d_i = 2 \rho_{\tau,\sigma}(y_i - \mu_i)$, the unweighted, un-summed term whose sum (optionally weighted) gives `deviance`. ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [y]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Observed response values. [mu]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Fitted mean values. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Per-observation deviance contributions, same shape as `y`. ::: ### [variance()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Variance function for `QuantileFamily`, identically equal to 1. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/feat-psis-loo/whittaker/families/quantile.py#L221-L239){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python variance(mu) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} `QuantileFamily` does not model a mean-variance relationship since fitting minimizes the ELF loss directly, so the family-specific variance function returns a constant array of ones regardless of `mu`; the working weights used during fitting instead come from `irls_update`. ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [mu]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Mean values on the response scale (unused beyond determining shape). ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Array of ones, same shape as `mu`. :::
